evidence.location: Complete reports/current.md, lines 1-340, read in continuous segments 1-90, 91-180, 181-270 and 271-340; complete assignment research brief, lines 1-36, effective requirements R_TASK/R_LANGUAGE/R_DATE, and the evidence-review instructions. Consequential checks focused on lines 11-76, 91-123, 137-172, 176-239 and 245-273.
evidence.basis: The verdict follows direct reading of the frozen source bodies and eight original charts/rendered pages, not acceptance of the author's ledger or self-assessment. CNNIC CP19 PDF p.7 and pp.61-62 and CP08 PDF p.40 and pp.73-75 support the 662m/664m figures, age-six-plus telephone-sampling population and weighting; the report does not claim statistically demonstrated zero growth. CSM MD003 body supports the adult-only denominator, 70.2% reach, 84.2% willingness and 71.8% having watched paid dramas, and the report correctly separates these from measured paying conversion. Direct inspection of CP17 p.6 confirms 335m apps, 427m WeChat and a 718m deduplicated union with the unequal selection rules; p.18 supports the policy-summary attribution. CP24 users/time/apps original images and CP16 category/ranking/overlap original images confirm the 851m three-channel union, separate 472m content reach, 13.0/26.9 hours, 62.0/125.6 uses, 487m category MAU, 429.69m Hongguo, 156.35m Lüpao Pao, 8.34m Xifan and the stated year-on-year/overlap figures. The report treats 73m as excess memberships rather than unique overlapping people, and does not infer acquisition attribution from co-use. MD006 pp.2-3, MD012 p.19, MD010's actual release and MD009 pp.6-7/14 support the monetary estimates, forecast labels, output-value distinction, deduplicated production estimate, ordinary budget range and 66.3% forecast. CP12, CP14, CP01, CP02, MD005 and MD008 original financial tables support every row of the consolidated financial comparison and the selected segment, promotion-expense and cash-flow claims; CP12's explicit reclassification and CP13's CMS governance/deconsolidation passages support the stated comparability and consolidation limits. CP20's retained official-release text supports the Kuaishou supply and marketing-spend claims, without establishing supplier profitability. MD014, CP25, CP26, MD006 p.6 and CP27 support the selected reward-withdrawal, third-party catalog, partnership and settlement mechanisms with their stated source status. MD004's complete statutory text, CP04, CP05, CP09, CP21 and CP03 support the definition, dates, classification thresholds, review obligations and campaign chronology. CP18 and CP22 support the distinction between the platform's minor-refund rule and civil-capacity law; CP10 retained statutory passages and CP11 court-published case support the other checked consumer and copyright claims. I read calculations.py lines 1-78 and calculation-output.json lines 1-490 without executing either. Formula/denominator tracing, arithmetic inspection and reconciliation to the displayed report found no discrepancy in the paid waterfall, conversion/CAC table, refund/budget sensitivity, free-viewing allocations and active-day table, break-even thresholds, reward-removal threshold or hybrid displaced-ad subtraction. The report explicitly labels their commercial inputs as assumptions and does not promote scenario profit into an observed industry margin. No required factual or calculation correction was identified. The execution record gives the actual source line ranges and hashes; this is not a claim to have read all pages of all 39 source records. CP10/CP20 were checked as retained official-web text, not newly retrieved complete websites; CP23 is an access-failure record and supports no substantive report claim. No other-language report, other reviewer result or author self-check was consulted.
